title: Isolation of Supernumerary Mini-Chromosomes from Fungi for Enrichment Sequencing
author: Thorsten Langner
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9t7h6rn
materials: Immediately after mixing, pipette protoplast mix into Bio-Rad plug mould (#1703713) and let solidify on ice for at least 30 min. Make sure to proceed quickly before the gel can solidify. Tip: Pipette the liquid gel while keeping the tube in the water bath. Mix briefly by pipetting up and down twice and directly transfer the solution in the plug mould. Alternatively, prepare protoplast/agarose gel mix in 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube and cut to size after the mix has solidified. For DNA extraction more than one plug might be required.

steps.title: Grow initial culture
steps.instruction: Plate a fresh culture of *M. oryzae* on complete medium agar plates and incubate at 24 °C for 7 days.

steps.title: Inoculate liquid YG medium
steps.instruction: In a 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask add 150 mL YG medium and inoculate with eight ~0.5 × 0.5 cm pieces of the 7‑day‑old mycelium; shake at 120 rpm, 24 °C for 3 days.

steps.title: Filter mycelium and remove media
steps.instruction: Filter the culture through two layers of Miracloth into a 50 mL Falcon tube (or 100 mL beaker); place the Miracloth in a funnel over a bottle to collect the filtrate and gently squeeze the mycelial mat to remove residual media.

steps.title: Prepare lysing enzyme solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysing enzyme solution as described in the methods and filter‑sterilise it before use.

steps.title: Add enzyme to mycelium
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL of the sterilised lysing enzyme solution to the collected mycelium.

steps.title: Generate protoplasts on shaker
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a horizontal shaker at room temperature, shake at 30 rpm for 2–4 h, and monitor protoplast formation microscopically.

steps.title: Filter protoplast suspension
steps.instruction: Pass the protoplast suspension through two layers of Miracloth into a 50 mL Falcon tube, using a funnel to collect the flow‑through.

steps.title: First centrifugation of protoplasts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the flow‑through at 1500 rpm, room temperature, for 10 min; carefully discard the supernatant with a pipette without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Wash protoplast pellet twice
steps.instruction: Add 25 mL of 1 M Sorbitol to the pellet, centrifuge again under the same conditions, discard supernatant, and repeat the wash once more (total of two washes).

steps.title: Resuspend protoplasts gently
steps.instruction: After the washes, remove as much supernatant as possible with a pipette, then add 100–200 µL of 1 M Sorbitol/50 mM EDTA and resuspend the fragile protoplasts using a cut 1 mL tip, pipetting very slowly or shaking gently.

steps.title: Assess protoplast concentration
steps.instruction: Examine the suspension under a microscope with a hemocytometer; aim for a concentration of approximately 3 × 10⁹ protoplasts · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Embed protoplasts in agarose plugs
steps.instruction: Mix one‑third volume of the protoplast suspension with two‑thirds volume of 1 % megabase agarose prepared in 1 M Sorbitol/50 mM EDTA at 45 °C; prepare the agarose in advance and keep it in a 55 °C water bath until use, then cast the mixture into plugs.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion of plugs
steps.instruction: Transfer each protoplast‑agarose plug to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, add 1 mL NDS buffer containing 200 µg · mL⁻¹ proteinase K, and incubate at 50 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: EDTA washing of plugs
steps.instruction: Remove the NDS buffer, add 1 mL fresh 50 mM EDTA, and shake slowly at room temperature for 30 min–1 h; repeat this wash three times. Washing may be performed on a thermomixer set to 22 °C, 200 rpm.

substeps.instruction: Repeat wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Store plugs before CHEF
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the final EDTA solution and store the plugs in NDS buffer (without proteinase K) at 4 °C until CHEF electrophoresis.

steps.title: Prepare agarose CHEF gel
steps.instruction: Make a 1 % megabase agarose gel in 0.5 % TAE or TBE buffer and allow it to solidify; use TBE for better resolution of large chromosomes and TAE when the DNA will be extracted for library preparation (note that borate in TBE can inhibit downstream enzymes).

steps.title: Load plugs and size markers
steps.instruction: Place each agarose plug into a well of the CHEF gel, add size markers (commercial *S. cerevisiae* and *S. pombe* chromosomes, Bio‑Rad #1703633 and #1703605).

steps.title: Run CHEF electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel on a Bio‑Rad CHEF‑DRII system with the following settings: initial switch interval 120 s, end switch interval 3600 s, voltage 1.8–2 V·cm⁻¹, run time 96 h, temperature 14 °C. Pre‑cool the circulating buffer to 14 °C for at least 30 min and avoid moving the system during the run.

steps.title: Stain and visualize DNA
steps.instruction: Immerse the gel in 1 µg · mL⁻¹ ethidium bromide (in 0.5 % buffer) for 30 min, then wash in 0.5 % TAE or TBE buffer for 10 min and view the bands on a UV transilluminator.

steps.title: Excise target bands
steps.instruction: Cut the desired chromosome bands from the gel with a scalpel, place each slice into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, keep at 4 °C, and remove as much excess gel as possible, ensuring clean edges to avoid agarose contamination in later steps.

steps.title: Moisturize D‑Tube dialyzer
steps.instruction: Moisturise a D‑Tube Dialyzer Midi 3.5 kDa MWCO (Merck #71506) with 800 µL ddH₂O for 1 min and inspect the membrane for leaks.

steps.title: Load gel slice into D‑Tube
steps.instruction: Remove the water with a pipette, place the agarose gel slice into the dialyzer chamber without touching the membrane with the pipette tip.

steps.title: Fill D‑Tube and assemble
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 % TAE buffer to the chamber, close the lid tightly, insert the dialyzer into the D‑Tube Electroelution Accessory Kit (Merck #71511) and place the assembly in an electrophoresis chamber.

steps.title: Electroelute DNA from gel
steps.instruction: Run electroelution in 0.5 % TAE buffer at 90 V for 3 h at room temperature, with the membrane facing the direction of migration; DNA will migrate into the buffer while some may adhere to the membrane.

steps.title: Recover and concentrate DNA
steps.instruction: Pipette up and down near the membrane to resuspend the eluted DNA, avoiding contact with the membrane or gel slice; transfer the solution to a 1.5 mL tube and concentrate in a speed‑vac to a final volume of 20–50 µL. Measure DNA concentration fluorometrically; 0.5 ng · µL⁻¹ is sufficient for low‑input library preparation.

steps.title: Prepare low‑input sequencing library
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s protocol for the Nextera low‑input library preparation kit (Illumina) using custom barcoding primers; the resulting library can be sequenced on a NextSeq 500 system.

steps.title: Concentrate DNA for library prep
steps.instruction: If necessary, further concentrate the DNA solution to 20–50 µL in a speed‑vac; verify that the final concentration meets the ≥0.5 ng · µL⁻¹ requirement before proceeding to library construction.
